questions.question: Consider the reaction: PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g). If the pressure of the system is increased at constant temperature, how will the equilibrium position change?

questions.question: For the reaction: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH = -198 kJ/mol. To maximize the yield of SO₃, which conditions would be most favorable?

This is the correct combination of conditions to maximize SO₃ yield.

questions.explanation: The reaction is exothermic (ΔH = -198 kJ/mol), so low temperature favors the forward reaction (product formation). On the reactant side, there are 2+1=3 moles of gas, and on the product side, there are 2 moles of gas. High pressure favors the side with fewer moles of gas, which is the product side. Thus, low temperature and high pressure maximize SO₃ yield.

questions.question: For the dissociation of calcium carbonate: CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g), ΔH > 0. Which of the following changes will increase the concentration of CO₂(g) at equilibrium?

options.explanation: Neither I nor II affects the concentration of CO₂(g).
This is the correct option; only increasing the temperature will increase the concentration of CO₂(g).
IV (decreasing the volume) actually decreases the concentration of CO₂(g).
I and II do not affect the concentration of CO₂(g), so this option is incorrect.

questions.explanation: I. Adding more CaCO₃(s) will not affect the equilibrium because the concentration of pure solids is considered constant and does not appear in the equilibrium constant expression. So, CO₂ concentration is unchanged. II. Removing solid CaO(s) will not affect the equilibrium for the same reason as I. So, CO₂ concentration is unchanged. III. The reaction is endothermic (ΔH > 0). Increasing the temperature will shift the equilibrium to the right to absorb the added heat, thus increasing the concentration of CO₂(g). IV. Decreasing the volume of the container will increase the pressure. Since there is only 1 mole of gas on the product side and 0 moles on the reactant side (solids), increasing the pressure (by decreasing volume) will shift the equilibrium to the left to reduce the pressure, thereby *decreasing* the concentration of CO₂(g). Therefore, only increasing the temperature will increase the concentration of CO₂(g).
